text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Vietnamese and Chinese delegates have discussed in Beijing measures aimed at quickening progress in talks over the delineation of sea borders in the Tonkin Gulf.
-- The National Assembly's Standing Committee has changed regulations on income tax setting a new minimum threshold for payment and abolishing an ordinance on irregular remittances from abroad.
-- Prime minister Vo Van Kiet has called for a nationwide campaign to mobilise people to build the country's infrastructure and to make full use of idle labour.
-- Consumer prices increased by one percent during the week ahead of the Tet lunar new year festival -- the lowest level for the period in several years.
-- Vietnam expects a trade deficit of about $4.3 billion in 1997.
-- Urban unemployment fell during 1996 to 5.88 percent while rural underemployment also dropped to 26.58 percent.
